why.title: Why EN 16931 now
why.p1: A PDF invoice is a picture of the data. The recipient's software cannot read the total or the VAT from it without text recognition. A structured document carries the same data in named fields: BT-1 is the number, BT-2 is the date, BT-3 is the document type.
why.p2: According to the bill as introduced, mandatory structured e-invoices between companies and to the state start on 1 July 2028. A PDF on its own is not a structured e-invoice. The documents you issue in Fakturist now are already in these formats too.

einvoicing2028.title: E-invoicing in Bulgaria from 2028: a guide for companies
einvoicing2028.summary: According to bill no. 52-602-01-60 amending the VAT Act, as introduced, structured e-invoices become mandatory between companies and to the state from 1 July 2028. The invoice will be a document in UBL 2.1 or CII under EN 16931, not a PDF. The bill has passed only a first reading, on 12 November 2026, so the text may change.

q1.title: What does the bill provide?
q1.p1: The bill provides for mandatory structured e-invoices between companies (B2B) and to the state (B2G) from 1 July 2028. They will travel over the CEF eDelivery AS4 network in UBL 2.1 and CII under EN 16931.
q1.p2: The issuer will send the invoice only to the recipient's address in the register the bill creates. There will be accredited providers and certified software. The conditions for them will be set in an ordinance.

q2.title: What are the dates?
q2.p1: The dates below follow the text as introduced. The ordinance is not out yet, so its deadline is a provision, not a fact.

q3.title: What is a structured e-invoice?
q3.p1: A structured e-invoice is a document in which every item of data sits in a named field that software can read without text recognition. A PDF is not such a document: it displays the data, it does not describe it.
q3.p2: The EN 16931 standard gives every field a code. Here is an excerpt of an invoice in UBL 2.1, with the field codes in the left column:
q3.bt1: Invoice number. Ten digits, no gaps (Art. 114(1)(2) VAT Act).
q3.bt3: Document type. 380 is an invoice, 381 is a credit note.

q4.title: What happens to the recipient?
q4.p1: According to the text as introduced, the recipient loses the input VAT credit if there is no structured e-invoice. So it is not only issuers who need to be ready: companies that only receive invoices will also want the documents in this form.

q5.title: How will the invoice be sent?
q5.p1: The issuer will send only to the recipient's address in the register the bill creates, over the CEF eDelivery AS4 network. The details of the register and of the providers will be in the ordinance. Those conditions are not published yet.

q6.title: What is still unclear?
q6.p1: The ordinance with the conditions for accredited providers and certified software is not out yet. According to the text as introduced, its deadline is 1 July 2027. No approval from the National Revenue Agency exists today, and Fakturist does not claim one. Nor do we claim to meet requirements that have not been set.

q7.1: Check your numbering: ten digits and no gaps. Art. 114(1)(2) of the VAT Act already requires it.
q7.2: Ask your accountant and your software provider whether they will issue UBL 2.1 or CII, not only PDF.
q7.3: Keep counterparty data accurate: company ID, VAT number and address. A structured document carries them in separate fields.
q7.4: Follow the ordinance and the text at the second reading. The conditions for providers and software will decide what is needed.
q7.title: What should a company do now?

q8.title: What does Fakturist already do today?
q8.p1: Every document is issued as both UBL 2.1 and CII under EN 16931, the free plan included. Not available yet, but planned: {planned}.

proforma.title: Pro forma invoice online
proforma.summary: A pro forma invoice is a request for payment, not a tax document. In Fakturist you make it from the same form as an invoice, send it as a PDF by email and, once the customer pays, turn it into an invoice without re-entering anything. Pro formas are included in every plan, the free one too.

1.title: What is a pro forma invoice?
1.p1: A document asking the customer to pay before you issue an invoice — for example for a prepayment or an offer with concrete amounts. It is not a tax document under the VAT Act: it has no date of the taxable event, does not go into the sales ledger and does not replace the invoice.

2.title: How do I make a pro forma in Fakturist?

steps.1: Open “New document” and choose the type “Pro forma invoice”.
steps.2: Fill in the buyer, the lines and the payment due date — as for an invoice.
steps.3: Save: the pro forma gets its own “ПФ-” number and a PDF that says it is not a tax document.
steps.4: Send it by email to the customer from its page or download the PDF.

3.title: How does a pro forma become an invoice?
3.p1: When the customer pays, press “Issue invoice” on the pro forma and choose the type: “Invoice” if the goods or service have already been delivered, or “Prepayment invoice” if the payment comes before delivery. The form is filled in from the pro forma; check the dates — for an advance it is the day the payment was received. On issuing, the pro forma is marked as invoiced and the invoice takes its number from the invoice series.

4.title: Pro forma or advance invoice?
4.p1: If you receive a payment before you deliver the goods or service, you issue an invoice for the advance within the statutory deadline after receiving it — the pro forma does not replace it. If you are VAT-registered, the tax as a rule becomes chargeable when the advance is received; if you are not, the advance invoice carries no VAT. In Fakturist choose the type “Prepayment invoice”; in the final invoice you deduct the advance by entering its number. Check advances on intra-Community supplies, reverse-charge cases and other special cases with your accountant.

link.text: How invoices go into the sales ledger

1.q: Is a pro forma a tax document?
1.a: No. It is a request for payment. The tax document is the invoice you issue after the payment or the delivery.

2.q: Does a pro forma go into the sales ledger?
2.a: No. Only invoices and notes go into the VAT ledgers.

3.q: Can I send the pro forma by email?
3.a: Yes — as a PDF, from the pro forma’s page. If your company has an email in its settings, the customer’s reply goes to it.

4.a: Pro formas are included in every plan, the free one too.

vatLedgers.title: VAT sales and purchase ledgers
vatLedgers.summary: Fakturist builds the sales ledger (PRODAGBI.TXT) from the invoices and notes you issue, and the purchase ledger (POKUPKI.TXT) from e-invoices you receive as XML. The files follow Annex 12 to the VAT Act Implementing Regulation, and what cannot be decided automatically is in a separate list for manual entry. Check them with the NRA’s program before filing; the company files the return.

list.1: The sales ledger for the month — from the invoices, credit and debit notes issued.
list.2: The purchase ledger — from e-invoices received as XML and documents in the inbox. Invoices received as PDF or on paper are entered in your accounting program.
list.3: The files use the encoding and record length from the NRA’s description, with amounts in euro.
list.4: Cancelled documents are reflected according to the month of cancellation.

2.title: What is entered automatically and what by hand?
2.p1: The usual cases (20 % and 9 % rates, zero rate, exempt supplies, intra-Community supplies) are entered on their own. Cases where the right field depends on facts outside the invoice — for example another rate, imports or reverse charge from a foreign supplier — are not guessed but go to the “for manual entry” list with the reason.

3.title: Who files the return?
3.p1: The company or its accountant — Fakturist files nothing with the NRA. Check the files with the NRA’s program before filing. Fakturist is not approved or certified by the NRA; no such approval for invoicing software exists today.

4.title: How does it work with an accounting firm?
4.p1: An accounting firm with an active mandate opens the client company’s ledgers from its own account and downloads them for the month, without you sending files.

1.a: The VAT ledgers are on the company’s “VAT ledgers” page in every plan.

2.q: Can I change the month of a received invoice?
2.a: Yes, up to 12 months after it was issued, as the VAT Act allows, and mark whether you have a right to input tax credit.

3.q: What about a copy of the same invoice?
3.a: If the same invoice is both in “Incoming” and in the inbox, both go to the manual-entry list until you reject one — they are not entered twice.

saft.title: SAF-T data from your invoices
saft.summary: SAF-T is a monthly file of accounting data under the NRA’s schema. Fakturist does not file SAF-T, but it gives you the sales for the month as five files under the SAF-T schema, version 1.0.3 — for the accounting program that assembles and files the whole file. The feature is in the plans {safTPlans}.

1.title: What is SAF-T?
1.p1: The Standard Audit File for Tax: a monthly XML with accounting data — the general ledger, customers, suppliers, invoices and payments. It is being introduced in stages; check on the NRA’s website when it becomes mandatory for your company.

list.1: SalesInvoices — the invoices and notes issued in the month.
list.2: Customers — the customers from those documents.
list.4: TaxTable and UOMTable — the tax codes and units of measure under the NRA’s nomenclatures.
list.5: The files are checked automatically against the SAF-T XSD, version 1.0.3, with every Fakturist update. Check them with the NRA’s tools before filing.

3.title: What does Fakturist not do?
3.p1: It does not file SAF-T and does not build the whole file: that needs the general ledger, purchases and balances, which live in the accounting program. Codes that cannot be determined from the invoice are not guessed but go to a list for manual review.

link.text: The VAT ledgers from the same invoices

4.title: How does the data reach the accountant?

steps.1: Open the company’s “SAF-T data” and choose the month.
steps.2: If needed, set the chart-of-accounts accounts and the related parties — the accountant does this.
steps.3: Download the files and load them into the accounting program that files SAF-T.

1.a: No. The company files it through its accounting program. Fakturist gives the sales data in its format.

2.a: XSD 1.0.3 — the current version of the SAF-T schema in Bulgaria, with the nomenclatures of its Annex 2.
